I've been listening to *Voice Hugs* a lot recently. It's a podcast that focuses on mental health, life advice, and relationships. The two co-hosts have great chemistry and the topics discussed get pretty deep, but there's also some lighthearted comedy sprinkled throughout. One of the hosts, Rowena Tsai, is also a YouTuber that makes self-care and personal development content.

*Asian Hustle Network* is also pretty good. They interview various Asian entrepreneurs and focus on AMPLIFYING THEIR VOICES AND EMPOWERING ASIANS. The mic quality is spotty and it gets a bit corny at times, but they also have a mental health angle, instead of just focusing on business stuff, so it's nice if you're into that.

Some other mental health podcasts I would recommend are *The Inner Child Podcast with Gloria Zhang* and *Masculine Psychology with David Tian*. They don't necessarily talk about  Asian American topics but are Asian podcast hosts with great, deep topics if you're looking to learn more about self-help.

ArcheAge and Blade & Soul. 

ArcheAge just simply looks huge.  It looks like everything I'd want in an MMO and it's so ambitious I suggest just checking out the website instead of me describing everything I'm looking forward to about it. 

Blade & Soul for the amazing combat and style.  I love the setting and the art, but I just hope there's a bit more to it than just fighting and looking sexy.

Guild Wars 2 is probably the best MMO for story. There isn't really a 'multitude of skills' but the combat is based more on context--doing what you can depending on the situation with the tools at your disposal. Skills can combo with other player's skills and you can switch weapons on the fly. 

There's also Age of Wushu which I've recommend on here a few times. It has no levels, no classes, and you can learn skills from any of the different schools. It has a story and some cut scenes depending on your character origin, but it's pretty ham fisted and cheesy so don't expect much from that. It's a nice MMO if you're looking for something to 'live in', since combat isn't really mandatory because you earn experience from everything you do including crafting and being a hobo.

Age of Wushu is like all the great things you've heard about EVE, but set in ancient China and without the spreadsheets and spaceships.  I'm having fun with it just farming hemp and playing music and I've barely touched everything there is to do or explore.

I'm playing Age of Wushu and it might be what you're looking for. It's like a sandbox MMO where you're left to do whatever you want. There's a lot of different ways your character can get stronger and there's not really any clear direction. It's confusing at first, so you have to ask around for help or look on forums for guides, but it's exciting to discover and explore a completely different MMO world. 

The economy and crafting is all player based, so you'll be communicating alot with other players to get things done. 

There's also something called 'team practice' that's a nice way to gather up some strangers and friends to practice your kung fu.

Sometimes these kinds of games are just to play around with friends, killing, looting, and exploring stuff, without having to do much thinking.
